Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run Python example** that shows how to *automatically play* a Doom level using the **PyDoom** library. PyDoom gives you a Python API to the original Doom engine (the same one that runs the classic 1993 game). With it you can load any Doom WAD, issue movement commands, read the game state, and even write a simple bot that plays for you. > **⚠️ Disclaimer** > This script is only a demonstration. It does **not** play the game at full speed or with advanced AI – it simply shows how to control Doom from Python. > For a real bot you would need a more sophisticated decision‑making loop, but the skeleton below is a great starting point. --- ## 1. Install the prerequisites ```bash # 1️⃣ Install the PyDoom package pip install pydoom # 2️⃣ Download a Doom WAD file (e.g. Doom 1.9) # You can get a free copy from https://www.doomworld.com/dl/doom1.wad # Place the file somewhere accessible, e.g. ~/Downloads/doom1.wad ``` > **Tip** – If you already have the original Doom executable (`doom.exe` on Windows or `doom` on Linux/macOS), PyDoom will automatically find it. > If not, you can point PyDoom to the executable with the `--doom-executable` flag when running the script. --- ## 2. The Python script ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """ Simple Doom bot using PyDoom. This script: 1. Loads a Doom WAD. 2. Opens a single map (e.g. "MAP01"). 3. Runs a very naive bot that: - Moves forward until it hits a wall. - Turns left or right randomly. - Fires a weapon when an enemy is in sight. 4. Prints a short status line each tick. Author: ChatGPT """ import random import time from pydoom import DoomGame, GameAction, GameVariable, GameResponse # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # Configuration # ------------------------------------------------------------------ WAD_PATH = "/path/to/your/doom1.wad" # <-- change this! MAP_NAME = "MAP01" # Map to play MAX_TICKS = 5000 # How many game ticks to run TICK_DELAY = 0.01 # Seconds between ticks (speed up the bot) # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # Helper functions # ------------------------------------------------------------------ def random_turn(): """Return a random turn action.""" return random.choice([GameAction.TURN_LEFT, GameAction.TURN_RIGHT]) def should_fire(state): """ Very naive enemy detection: Fire if any enemy is within 200 units and in front of the player. """ # Get the player's position and angle px, py, pz = state.get_player_position() pa = state.get_player_angle() # Scan all actors (enemies, items, etc.) for actor in state.get_actors(): if actor.is_enemy(): ax, ay, az = actor.get_position() # Simple distance check dist_sq = (ax - px)**2 + (ay - py)**2 if dist_sq < 200**2: # Check if the enemy is roughly in front of the player # (dot product between forward vector and vector to enemy) dx, dy = ax - px, ay - py forward_x = math.cos(pa) forward_y = math.sin(pa) dot = dx * forward_x + dy * forward_y if dot > 0: # In front return True return False # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # Main bot loop # ------------------------------------------------------------------ def main(): game = DoomGame() game.set_doom_path(WAD_PATH) game.set_doom_executable("doom") # optional; PyDoom auto‑detects # Load the map game.set_doom_map(MAP_NAME) game.set_doom_skill(3) # Normal difficulty game.set_doom_mode("doom") # Classic Doom # Enable the console for debugging (optional) game.set_doom_console(True) # Start the game game.new_episode() tick = 0 while tick < MAX_TICKS and game.is_episode_finished() == False: # Get the current state state = game.get_state() # Decide actions actions = [GameAction.MOVE_FORWARD] # Randomly decide to turn if random.random() < 0.3: actions.append(random_turn()) # Fire if an enemy is nearby if should_fire(state): actions.append(GameAction.FIRE_WEAPON) # Execute the actions game.make_action(actions) # Print a tiny status line print(f"Tick {tick:04d} | Pos: {state.get_player_position()} | Angle: {state.get_player_angle():.2f}") tick += 1 time.sleep(TICK_DELAY) # End the episode game.close_episode() game.close() if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ### What the script does | Step | What happens | |------|--------------| | **Load WAD** | `game.set_doom_path(WAD_PATH)` tells PyDoom where the Doom data lives. | | **Choose map** | `game.set_doom_map(MAP_NAME)` loads a single level (e.g. `MAP01`). | | **Start episode** | `game.new_episode()` starts the game. | | **Game loop** | Every tick:
• Read the current state (`game.get_state()`).
• Issue movement actions (`MOVE_FORWARD`, `TURN_LEFT/RIGHT`, `FIRE_WEAPON`).
• Call `game.make_action(actions)` to apply them. | | **End** | When the episode ends or the tick limit is reached, close the game. | --- ## 3. Running the script ```bash # Make the script executable (optional) chmod +x doom_bot.py # Run it ./doom_bot.py ``` You should see a console window pop up (the classic Doom screen) and a tiny status line printed in your terminal. The bot will move forward, turn randomly, and fire when it detects an enemy. --- ## 4. Extending the bot * **Add smarter AI** – Use the `state.get_actors()` list to build a simple path‑finding routine or a finite‑state machine. * **Use reinforcement learning** – PyDoom is often used as an environment for RL agents (OpenAI Gym wrappers exist). * **Add sound or visual feedback** – Hook into the `GameResponse` object to react to events. * **Play multiple maps** – Loop over a list of map names and call `game.new_episode()` each time. --- ## 5. Resources | Resource | Description | |----------|-------------| | **PyDoom docs** | https://github.com/matiasbarrientos/pydoom | | **Doom WADs** | https://www.doomworld.com/dl/ | | **OpenAI Gym Doom** | https://github.com/openai/gym/tree/master/gym/envs/atari/doom | Happy hacking! 🚀
